d010ad1b3aa96922fec0834183b8824882bd2c97.notes: Used the recorded row-0 header, which gives clean full column names. e26bf628169d3aecf4e1052362a421c16a630da8.notes: Threshold 500 taken from the title ('Spend over £500 in the UK Commission for Employment and Skills'). 'Date' includes a literal time component in the sample ('10/01/2014 00:00') — always midnight in samples shown, so date extraction should be safe, but reviewer should confirm. No expense_area-equivalent column exists (only department-level 'Department Family'/'Entity'), so left unmapped. Table also carries 'Year' and 'Period' columns, but sample values ('C', '12') don't read as a clean, publishable period label, so 'period' was left unmapped — reviewer should check what these encode before adding. 'Supplier' values carry an embedded supplier code prefix (e.g. 'ASP002 - Aspero Limited') — kept exactly as published, not split apart. Not mapped, no schema slot: Supplier postcode, Supplier type, HOME_CREDIT, HOME_DEBIT, Contract Number, Project Code, Expenditure type. Review: no dates or expense area in the source; Year/Period columns opaque and left unmapped. Layouts: 7 added: Oct-2011 'Pay Period/Pay Date/Pay Value/Supplier' layout (7 files) has an apparently mislabeled header — the sample data shows the 'Pay Period' column holding the payment date and the 'Pay Date' column holding the numeric amount, with 'Pay Value' a constant 'PAY' marker; mapped by data position rather than label, reviewer should double-check; Nov-2011 same-shape layout (5 files) covered by that same mapping; Jan-2014 detailed BIS layout already covered by the existing columns; Apr-Dec-2013 detailed BIS layout (space-padded ' Amount ', 4 files) already covered; Nov-2012 layout (1 file) with correctly labelled 'Pay Date'/'Pay Value' columns added; one 2013 BIS layout (1 file) using 'Transaction Number' in place of 'tran_ref' added; skipped one 'Supplier'/'Gross Value' totals-only layout (64 rows, per-supplier totals not per-payment lines). Review 2026-09-06: the 2011-12 monthly files carry mislabelled headers: the date sits under 'Pay Period', the amount under 'Pay Date' and a literal 'PAY' under 'Pay Value' (sample row ' 20-Oct-11', '527.11', 'PAY', supplier); the second alternate layout maps them by content. The May 2012 file has only Supplier and Gross Value, so those 64 rows carry no date or period.

'merchant_category' (e.g. 'Legal Fees & Charges', 'Home Care') is used for expense_type as the closest categorical field; 'department' (e.g. 'Adults', 'City Developments and Neighbourhood') is used for expense_area. c9177a5a76909e19b03b336a53a1627b643be0b1.notes: The brief lists 8 layout entries for the 60 files, but only 2 distinct header-naming schemes among them; the other 6 are the same two schemes with a varying number of extra, empty-header trailing columns (column_count 19/21/29/30/40 vs 7), evidently trailing commas in some quarterly exports rather than real extra fields — none of them carry any header text, so nothing is lost by leaving them unmapped. 'columns' covers the 'Service Area'/'Expense Type'/'Invoice Payment Date' naming (45 files: the 36-file primary layout plus the three same-named padded layouts, 3+3+3 files); 'alt_columns' covers the 'Service Label'/'Expense Category'/'Date' naming (15 files: 11 plus the three same-named padded layouts, 2+1+1 files). 'Body Name' is always literally 'TfGM' in the sample rows and is not mapped; constants.body uses the brief's full publisher name instead, matching the convention in the other reviewed entries. No description/period source column is available in either layout. Review 2026-09-07: 60 quarterly files, April 2011 to March 2026, two header schemes. Credits are published in accounting brackets, '(2,586.20)', and are read as negative amounts; five rows with a blank amount are held.

486018dd852f32dded2fa96788e960b215d0c74c.notes: Two layouts in the brief differ only by three trailing columns present in one (ObjectId, _lon, _lat) and absent in the other; every column used here has identical header text in both, so no alt_columns entry is needed. 'Date_Paid' and 'Date_Received' are both blank in every sampled row — payment_date will likely be null for most/all rows; kept as the semantically closer field to 'payment_date' (schema payment_date is not required). 'Customer_Supplier_Description' holds the actual supplier/contractor name (e.g. 'Urbaser Ltd', 'Tivoli Group Limited') despite its generic-sounding header, and is mapped to supplier. 'Service_Label' (e.g. 'Environmental and regulatory services', 'Planning Services') is used for expense_area over the more granular 'Division_Description' (e.g. 'Client Services (Depot)', 'Planning'); reviewer should check which is the better fit. 'Capital_Revenue' (Revenue/Capital flag) and the various *_Code/ObjectId/_lon/_lat columns have no matching schema column and are left unmapped. Title states 'Spend Over 250', so threshold_gbp is 250, not the family default of 500. Review 2026-09-07: Date_Paid and Date_Received are blank in every row, so payment_date is null and the period is taken from the title (financial year 2024 to 2025). The layer was fetched in three formats; one is kept.

VAT)'. 71 files, 6 header layouts by the brief's count, but only 3 distinct header-name schemes: 'columns' covers the April-2013-style (SUPPLIER NAME, blank col, PORTFOLIO, COST CENTRE, EXPENDITURE CLASS, POST. DATE, AMOUNT, REF., blank col; 5 files) and the April-2014-style (same names, no blank cols; 17 files) = 22 files. First alt_columns entry covers the April-2015-style naming (adds IRRECOVERABLE VAT, uses PROCLASS REF.; 10 files) and is also used by two title-row layouts whose header text is identical once you skip past the embedded title lines: the April-2017-style layout (31 files) and the August-2015-style layout with 'BLABY DISTRICT COUNCIL' on the title row (4 files) -- both have a blank/title row 0 with the real header six rows further down ('SUPPLIER NAME, PORTFOLIO, COST CENTRE, EXPENDITURE CLASS, POST. So the first alt_columns entry covers 10+31+4 = 45 files. COST CENTRE (a mid-level cost-centre field between PORTFOLIO and EXPENDITURE CLASS) has no schema slot and is left unmapped in every layout; IRRECOVERABLE VAT is never folded into amount_gbp, per the family rule. Review 2026-09-07: header_row 6 so the file-by-file header search (rows 0-9) finds the header under the title block in 35 files and on row 0 in the rest.

7176851ed784e350bbfb14a51dc871e5ea8f05f9.notes: Threshold 500 taken from the dataset title ('Payments to suppliers with a value over £500 from Bristol City Council'). All 61 files (59+1+1 per the brief's layout count) share the same header names -- 'Body', 'Body Name', 'Name', 'Amount', 'Pay Date', 'Transaction Number', 'Description 1', 'Description 2', 'Description 3' -- the two minority layouts only reorder 'Amount'/'Pay Date'/'Transaction Number' or add one blank trailing column, so no alt_columns entry is needed. 'Body' is always literally 'Bristol City council' and 'Body Name' is always an ordnance-survey doc URI in the samples; neither is mapped, constants.body is used instead. Three free-text description columns exist but the schema has only two slots (expense_type/expense_area and description): 'Description 1' reads as a broad category (e.g. 'Catering', 'Contract Cleaning', 'Acquisition of Buildings') and is mapped to expense_type; 'Description 2' reads as a more specific programme/purpose (e.g. 'Outdoor Education -Dean Fields', 'Capital - Temporary Accommodation (ITS) – GF Acquisitions Programme') and is mapped to description; reviewer should check whether Description 2 would suit expense_area better instead. 'Description 3' is blank or a single space in every sample row and is left unmapped. No expense_area source column is available under this reading. A separate 'tables' preview in the brief shows the same file with lowercase 'amount' and trailing-space description headers -- same columns, cosmetic case/spacing difference only, already covered by the mapping above.

1c32cca186ecbf2dbe371eb2225a99f8f550aa79.notes: Threshold 500 taken from the dataset title ('Payments to suppliers with a value over £500 from Cheltenham Borough Council'). (a separate supplier invoice number alongside the council's own 'TransactionNumber') has no second reference slot and is left unmapped. The May-2020 file (1 file) has a mislabelled header: its 'Expense Type' column actually holds free-text purpose ('R & M of Build Fire Systems') -- the same content that sits under 'Purpose' in the main layout -- while the true expense-type code (matching the main layout's 'Expense Type' values like 'R4445-HRA110') sits in a column with no header text at all; that blank-header code column and the equally unlabelled Organisation-Unit-equivalent column are left unmapped for this one file since they cannot be referenced by header text, so expense_area and expense_type are absent from the alt_columns entry -- reviewer should check whether the source file can be re-inspected for real column names. 11 + 1 = 12, matching files_extracted.

64990c73bdf6580c6bf8c8ebd66c2b7230b72f57.notes: Title is 'All Payments to Suppliers' with no threshold stated, but the resource filename itself is 'over250payments2026.csv' -- read as the return's own £250 threshold (York's standard transparency threshold), not a genuinely unfiltered export. Header text carries heavy fixed-width padding baked into the column names themselves (this is a plain-text/fixed-width export saved as CSV) -- mapped using the exact padded strings from the brief. The first sample row in every file is a literal dashed divider line ('--------...') repeating the fixed-width rule under the header -- not a real payment row -- reviewer/build should drop it (and any other divider/blank rows) before loading; this may recur elsewhere in the same file. 'Department Family' and 'Entity' hold constant 'DCMS'/'NHM' text in every row and are not mapped, constants.body is used instead (set to the brief's publisher name, the parent department, since the file's own 'Entity' value 'NHM' is not itself a government body name in the index's terms -- reviewer should check whether 'Natural History Museum' would be a better constants.body given every one of these five sources is NHM's own return). 'VAT Registration Number' is present (blank in every sample row) and is not an amount column, so it is left unmapped regardless. Review 2026-09-07: body is the Natural History Museum, the paying body; DCMS is the publisher of record on the row.

b94b9dc9b27903a7de2e6d82ae53b58f32779e45.notes: Threshold 500 from the title ('Payments to suppliers with a value over £500') and the resource filenames ('council-spending-over-500-...'). 68 files, 7 layouts in the brief, reduced to 5 distinct layouts for the columns actually used: 'columns' covers the 50-file 'Body/Body Name/Date/Transaction Number/Amount/Supplier Name/.../Expense Area/Expense Type/.../Extended Description' layout, which also silently covers 2 further 1-file layouts in the brief ('Organisation' instead of 'Body', 'Body Name ' with a trailing space, and Expense Code/Expense Type swapped in order) because every header this mapping actually reads from them (Date, Transaction Number, Amount, Supplier Name, Expense Area, Expense Type, Extended Description) is spelled identically -- no alt_columns entry needed for those two. alt_columns[0] is the single 2014 file with a wholly different 'Organisation/Company Name/Payment Date/Invoice No/Nett Amount/.../Responsible Unit Desc/Detailed Expenses Desc/.../Goods Description' naming. alt_columns[1]/[2] are the two later 'Organisation Name/.../Organisational Unit/.../Procurement Category (or Category)/.../Payment Date/Transaction Number/Amount (£)/Purpose' layouts (8 and 4 files); they differ only by a typo in the header used for expense_type ('Procurement Category' vs 'Procurement Catergory'), which is why both are kept as separate entries rather than merged. alt_columns[3] (3 files, e.g. media/4999) is plainly mislabelled: its 'Service Category URI' column holds short category text ('GM External Contractors', 'Adhoc Works For Burials') identical in style to what the other layouts call Expense Type/Procurement Category, not a URI, so expense_type is mapped from it by content, not by its label -- reviewer should double-check this reading. No period column in any layout. Reviewer should also confirm the DD/MM/YYYY date format is consistent across all 68 files, and that credits/negative amounts (seen in the Purpose-column layout, e.g. '-797.77') are genuine published credits.

3729b068e1be533026778ca2209a810dedfac017.reject: Both extracted files hold the same 5-column table (financial_year, date, percentage_paid_on_time, percentage_paid_between_31_60_days, percentage_paid_more_than_60_days): one row per month giving the percentage of invoices paid on time / 31-60 days / 60+ days. This is an aggregate payment-performance statistic, not a payment-line return -- no supplier, no individual amount, no per-payment date. Despite the CKAN title 'Accounts Payable - Supplier payments', the actual table is not this family.

425b7f4146e05b83577f39daa7ad902c25dddebe.notes: Threshold: this MHCLG series bundles two kinds of file under one dataset -- 'TP' transparency-payment exports (Date of Payment/Amount in Sterling, sometimes with Voluntary & Community Sector/SME Class/Sole Trader/Narrative columns) and 'GPC' government procurement card exports (Clearing/Amount, Doc Nbr, sometimes Item Text/Merchant category). One 2012/2013 file name literally says 'DCLG_expenditure_over__250' (over £250), but sample rows across both TP and GPC layouts in this and other years include payments well under £250 (e.g. £105.33, £117.48, £251) and GPC card purchases down to a few pounds (£7.18, £14.78, £17.80, £20.00) -- the release is not consistently filtered at any single floor. Treated as threshold_gbp 0 (all payments, no threshold), per the family convention for unthresholded returns. Reviewer should check whether the named-£250 file is actually threshold-filtered and, if so, whether it is worth separating out. 'columns'/'alt_columns' cover only the payment-line (TP) and card-transaction (GPC) layouts. Both families keep identical header text for the columns used here across every extra column seen in the brief (Voluntary & Community Sector, SME Class, Sole Trader, D-U-N-S Number, Postal Code, PSPES Level 2, Item, Purchasing Item Text, Profit Center, GPC Cardholder, Reference No/Ref No/Ref, and assorted trailing empty columns are all unmapped, no schema slot and/or not reliable) -- so those variants collapse into the same mapping rather than needing their own alt_columns entry. 'reference' always comes from 'Transaction number' (TP) or 'Doc Nbr' (GPC), not from the extra 'Reference No'/'Ref No'/'Ref' columns some later files carry, since those hold a small sequential index (e.g. '2'), not a real payment reference. expense_type is always the 'Expense Type' column (present in both families); 'Merchant category' (GPC only) is not mapped anywhere, since Expense Type already fills that role. description prefers 'Item Text' (GPC) or 'Narrative' (TP) where present; where neither exists, description is left unmapped rather than substituting 'Merchant category'. 2 of 5 files' layouts mapped. Of the dataset's 5 files, 3 are left unmapped and excluded from this proposal: 1 file ('Introduction' sheet) is a text cover page with no table at all; 2 files ('ALB/Supplier/Net Amount' and 'ALB Code/Public Sector Procurement Expenditure Survey Category/Supplier/Net Amount') are annual per-supplier expenditure totals -- one row per supplier for the whole year, not per-payment lines -- so they are aggregates, not this family, and were skipped rather than mapped.

eb7238984b4cab8b5dbbed9d55567bb252af3816.notes: No stated threshold in the title ('Payments to suppliers from Monmouthshire County Council'); sample amounts run as low as £18-£85, consistent with an unfiltered full payments export, so threshold_gbp is 0 per the family rule for a return with no stated threshold. Of the 19 files, 5 share this same 15-column header ('Service Area Categorisation' ... 'Customer ID') just at different row offsets (header_row 0, 1 or 2, plus varying counts of empty trailing columns) -- header_row is set to 2 and build.py's own row-search (0..header_row+3) finds the right row per file, so no alt_columns entries were needed for those. 13 of the 19 files (the single largest layout by file count) carry a corrupted header that leaked a raw SQL SELECT statement across the header row and, in every one of the brief's sampled rows below it, further JOIN-clause text -- not real data or a recognisable header -- so the true header/data start could not be determined and is left unmapped; those files will be held by the build with a 'no known layout fits' reason until someone opens one directly. One further file (5,879 rows) shows the 'Supplier Name' column holding the literal code '3663' for two consecutive sample rows before reverting to real names ('Aid-Call Ltd', 'Alexandra Workwear PLC', ...) -- this reads as the publisher's own data-quality noise (a supplier without a name on file), not a header/label mismatch, so it is kept as published rather than remapped. 'Narrative' is blank in every sampled row but is the file's only free-text field, so description will likely be sparse. Not mapped, no schema slot: Service Division Categorisation, Responsible Unit, Expense Code, Order ID, Capital/Revenue, Supplier ID, Customer ID.

e77fd05a12fb3fde1236a10a2e19856b8cdcab89.reject: a £25,000 transparency return ('NHS Norfolk and Suffolk ICB - 25k Expenditure Report'), a different series from spend over £500

fe0f24ae537424a01077820f688c32f5edc7d8ee.notes: No stated threshold in the title ('Payments to Suppliers - 2022 to 2023'); threshold_gbp is 0 per the family rule for a return with no stated threshold -- reviewer should check whether North Ayrshire's own transparency policy states a floor elsewhere, since Scottish councils typically publish this series under a stated threshold that this particular title does not repeat.
